findings.title: IAM policy allows all actions on all resources
findings.description: An Allow statement with Action "*" on Resource "*" is administrative access. Scope actions and resources to least privilege.
findings.evidence: policy = Allow statement with Action "*" on Resource "*"

findings.title: Inline admin policy attached to role/user/group
findings.description: An inline IAM policy with an Allow statement granting Action "*" (or "*:*") on Resource "*" is administrative access. Inline policies are harder to audit than managed ones; scope them to least privilege.
findings.evidence: policy = Allow statement with Action "*" (or "*:*") on Resource "*"
findings.remediation:
Move the inline admin policy to a scoped customer-managed policy (see
AEGIS-AWS-006 fix). Inline policies on identities are hard to audit — prefer
managed policies attached to groups/roles.

findings.title: IAM policy allows privilege escalation (create policy + attach policy)
findings.description: The policy combines a policy-authoring action (iam:CreatePolicy, iam:PutRolePolicy, iam:PutUserPolicy, iam:PutGroupPolicy) with a policy-attachment action (iam:AttachRolePolicy, iam:AttachUserPolicy, iam:AttachGroupPolicy). Attack path: create an administrative policy, attach it to your own role/user, assume full admin. Split authoring from attachment duties and scope each to least privilege.
findings.evidence: policy = Allow statements grant policy-authoring and policy-attachment actions
findings.expected: separate policy authoring from attachment; scope both to least privilege
findings.remediation:
Split policy authoring from attachment (this combination is the classic privilege
escalation primitive). Remove `iam:CreatePolicy*` / `iam:Attach*Policy` from the
workload policy. Policy management belongs in a separate, human-gated CI/CD role —
never in an application runtime role.

findings.title: IAM policy allows privilege escalation via iam:PassRole on * with compute launch
findings.description: The policy allows iam:PassRole on "*" together with a role-assumption primitive (ec2:RunInstances, lambda:CreateFunction, lambda:UpdateFunctionCode, ...). Attack path: launch a compute resource passing an administrative role, then steal its credentials from the instance metadata / environment. Scope iam:PassRole to specific role ARNs.
findings.evidence: policy = Allow statements grant iam:PassRole on "*" with a compute-launch primitive
findings.expected: scope iam:PassRole to specific role ARNs
findings.remediation:
Scope `iam:PassRole` to the exact role ARNs the workload must pass, and only
together with the specific compute-launch action it needs:
{
  "Effect": "Allow",
  "Action": "iam:PassRole",
  "Resource": "arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/AppExecutionRole"
}
Never grant `iam:PassRole` on `*` — it lets the holder escalate to any role.

findings.title: IAM policy allows data exfiltration primitives
findings.description: The policy grants a known exfiltration pair: s3:GetObject + s3:PutObject on "*" (copy data to an attacker bucket), rds:CreateDBSnapshot + rds:ModifyDBSnapshotAttribute (share a snapshot cross-account), or ec2:CreateSnapshot + ec2:ModifySnapshotAttribute (share an EBS snapshot). Attack path: snapshot or copy production data, share it outside the account. Scope data-plane actions to specific resources.
findings.evidence: policy = Allow statements grant exfiltration pair s3:GetObject + s3:PutObject on "*"
findings.expected: scope data-plane actions to specific resources
findings.remediation: Apply least privilege. Replace wildcard (`*`) actions and resources with the minimum scoped ARNs the workload needs. Split policy authoring from attachment. Use IAM Access Analyzer to generate scoped policies from CloudTrail history.

findings.title: IAM permissions management actions allowed on all resources
findings.description: An Allow statement grants IAM write actions (iam:Put*, iam:Create*, iam:Update*, iam:Delete*, iam:Attach*, iam:Detach*, or iam:*) on Resource "*". Attack path: modify any identity's policies directly to escalate to admin. Read-only IAM actions (iam:Get*, iam:List*, iam:Generate*, iam:Simulate*) are excluded. Scope IAM management to specific users, roles, and policies.
findings.evidence: policy = Allow statement grants IAM management action "*" on "*"
findings.expected: scope IAM management actions to specific identities
findings.remediation: Apply least privilege. Replace wildcard (`*`) actions and resources with the minimum scoped ARNs the workload needs. Split policy authoring from attachment. Use IAM Access Analyzer to generate scoped policies from CloudTrail history.

findings.title: IAM user uses an inline policy
findings.description: The user embeds an inline policy document instead of attaching a managed policy. Inline policies cannot be reused, versioned, or reviewed centrally. Prefer aws_iam_policy with aws_iam_user_policy_attachment.
findings.remediation: Apply least privilege. Replace wildcard (`*`) actions and resources with the minimum scoped ARNs the workload needs. Split policy authoring from attachment. Use IAM Access Analyzer to generate scoped policies from CloudTrail history.

findings.title: IAM user has no tags
findings.description: The IAM user carries no tags, making ownership, purpose, and lifecycle untraceable in audits and complicating attribute-based access control. Tag identities with at least owner and purpose.
findings.remediation: Apply least privilege. Replace wildcard (`*`) actions and resources with the minimum scoped ARNs the workload needs. Split policy authoring from attachment. Use IAM Access Analyzer to generate scoped policies from CloudTrail history.
